1.title: Know the words of social media management
1.intro: A social media manager plans, posts and watches content for a business.
pts: Learn the terms: platform, post, story, reach, engagement, follower, hashtag, call to action, content calendar.
Reach is how many people saw a post; engagement is how many acted.
Each platform has its own style and audience.
Follow five local business accounts and note what they post and how people respond.
1.ex: A café posts a photo of a new pastry with the line 'Fresh at 8 a.m. tomorrow.' Likes and comments show engagement.
1.act: Define ten terms and review five accounts.
1.std: Task: review five accounts. Condition: from public pages. Standard: each has audience, post types and one idea to improve.

2.title: Explain the workflow from plan to report
2.intro: Social media work follows steps. Name them to stay on schedule.
pts: The steps: goals, audience, content plan, create, schedule, post, reply, measure, report.
Set one goal at a time: more enquiries, more visits or more followers.
A content calendar lists date, platform, topic, text, image and status.
Agree who approves posts and how fast.
2.ex: Goal: 20 enquiries in a month. Plan: three posts a week with one clear action each.
2.act: Build a four-week content calendar for a pretend shop.
2.std: Task: build a calendar. Condition: from a brief. Standard: every row has date, platform, topic, text, image and approver.

3.title: Create and schedule posts to a standard
3.intro: Now you make. Write clear posts that serve the goal.
pts: Put the main point first. Use short words.
One post, one message, one action.
Add descriptive text for images so people using screen readers understand them.
Check spelling, links and facts before scheduling.
3.ex: Before: 'Big news!!!' After: 'New winter hours: open 8 to 4, Tuesday to Saturday. Visit us.'
3.act: Create and schedule a week of posts and ask a friend to find mistakes.
3.std: Task: create one week of posts. Condition: from a brief in three hours. Standard: each post has one message and action, image text is provided and no errors remain.

4.title: Follow Canadian rules for social media marketing
4.intro: Posts that sell are advertising. Rules apply.
pts: Advertising must be truthful. Do not post fake reviews or false claims.
Paid or gifted endorsements must be clearly disclosed.
Commercial messages by email or text need consent and an unsubscribe; check the current rule with the local authority.
Contests have rules; in some provinces they need extra steps. Check before you run one. Respect copyright and ask before using a person's photo.
4.ex: A client wants to repost a customer photo. You ask the customer for permission first and credit them.
4.act: Make a table of rule, who sets it, what you must do and where you checked, for ten post types.
4.std: Task: build a rules table. Condition: using official public pages. Standard: each row has a dated source; unclear items say 'check the current rule with the local authority'.

5.title: Price your service and check it pays
5.intro: You are paid for steady results and time.
pts: Time includes planning, creating, posting, replying and reporting.
Compare hourly, monthly package and per-post pricing.
A monthly package needs a clear list: posts, platforms, replies and report.
Track hours per client to see if the price is fair.
5.ex: A package of 12 posts and a report takes 14 hours at 45 USD: 630 USD a month. Teaching figures only.
5.act: Time a week of work and set a monthly package.
5.std: Task: price a monthly package. Condition: from your time log. Standard: hours, rate and package list are shown and a mentor can follow the numbers.

6.title: Measure results and report
pts: Choose a few measures tied to the goal: reach, clicks, enquiries.
Compare this month with last month.
Report in plain words: what happened, why, what we do next.
Do not claim the number of followers equals sales.
6.ex: Posts with a photo of the product got 3 times more clicks than text-only posts. Next month: more product photos.
6.act: Collect a month of data and write a one-page report.
6.std: Task: write a monthly report. Condition: from real or practice data. Standard: three measures, a cause for each change and two next steps.

7.title: Protect accounts, people and reputation
7.intro: A manager holds the keys to a brand voice. Be careful.
pts: Use strong passwords and two-step sign-in; give access by role and remove it when people leave.
Reply to comments politely. For complaints, move to a private channel and fix the problem.
Do not share customer information. Privacy law applies.
Write a short agreement: scope, fees, approvals, who owns the accounts and content, and how to end it.
7.ex: A customer complains in a comment. You reply: 'Sorry about that. Please message us your order number so we can fix it.'
7.act: Write an agreement and a response guide for ten comments.
7.std: Task: produce an agreement and a guide. Condition: reviewed by a mentor. Standard: scope, fees, approvals and ownership are in plain words.

8.title: Run a real account for 60 days and decide
8.intro: Now you run it, measure and decide.
pts: Set a goal for one real or practice account.
Record posts, hours, results and feedback each week.
Ask the client what changed.
Choose: stop, change or grow, and write a 12-month plan.
8.ex: After 60 days: 24 posts, 30 hours, enquiries up from 6 to 14 a month. You add a second client.
8.act: Run the pilot and present a 12-month plan to a panel of three.
8.std: Task: run a 60-day account pilot. Condition: real client and agreement. Standard: calendar kept, report written and the decision uses numbers.

quiz: What is the difference between reach and engagement?
Reach is how many saw a post; engagement is how many acted.
What does a content calendar list?
Date, platform, topic, text, image and status.
Why give one goal at a time?
It keeps the plan clear and measurable.
Why add image text for screen readers?
So everyone can understand the image.
What must be disclosed in a paid post?
That it is paid or gifted.
What do commercial messages by email need?
Consent and an unsubscribe; check the current rule.
How should you handle a public complaint?
Reply politely and move it to a private channel.
Why use two-step sign-in?
To protect the account if the password is stolen.
What do you compare in a report?
This month against last month.
What do you do when you do not know a rule?
Check the current rule with the local authority.
